name: Karakol Lakes (Iolgo)
full: Karakol Lakes — a cascade of 7 cirque lakes on the western slope of the Iolgo Range (the watershed of the Katun and Biya) at the foot of Bagatash Pass, in the upper reaches of the Elekmonar river (Sorgat tract)
elev: Sources differ: 1630–1840 m (iskatel) or from ~1820 m (lowest) to ~2097 m (highest) (Bolshaya Strana); a tour operator says 1620–2000 m
short: A chain of seven cold, clear lakes below Bagatash Pass on the Iolgo Range, connected by streams and small waterfalls — a classic one-day “all-terrain truck” outing from Elekmonar and Chemal.
desc: Seven lakes lie in steps in the cirques of the western slope of the Iolgo Range at an elevation of about 1600–2100 m, 300–800 m apart. The largest is the 5th lake (~435×350 m), where the only tourist base stands, with cedar cabins and a canteen; the smallest is the 7th (~78×30 m). The water is icy and very clean; in winter the small lakes freeze through, and there is almost no fish; on the upper lakes snow lies even in July. Higher up are Bagatash Pass with its panorama, the “Valley of Turs” (cairns) and the rock outliers called the “Castles of the Mountain Spirits”. The lakes are a natural monument of regional significance (since 1987, confirmed in 1996, IUCN category III). Access is from Elekmonar up the Elekmonar river valley with dozens of fords to the Sorgat tract (~3 h on a GAZ-66 “shishiga” or a UAZ), then 8–12 km on foot, on horseback or by the same all-terrain truck. The season runs from late May to October; in winter — snowmobile tours.
guide: You will ride in a “shishiga” along the bed of the Elekmonar — hold on tight, it is part of the adventure, not an inconvenience. Don't stop at the fifth lake with the tourist base: walk up the chain to the seventh and to Bagatash Pass — from there you can see all the lakes at once and half of Altai. According to legend, the lakes are beads of a pearl necklace of an evil spirit's daughter, and the spirits of the second lake help those who ask for health. Take a down jacket even in July: at night it can be zero here, and hail can come in the daytime.
see: All 7 lakes in the chain; Bagatash Pass (panorama); the “Valley of Turs” (cairns); the “Castles of the Mountain Spirits” outliers; small waterfalls between the lakes; the starry sky (Milky Way) if you stay overnight.
skip: You get carsick and are not ready for 3–4 hours of shaking in an all-terrain truck each way for a few hours at the lakes, or you have only one day and want more views for less travel — then choose Chemal and the Katun.
diff: Moderate. A one-day trip by all-terrain truck is physically not hard, but the road is exhausting (up to 4 h each way). On foot from Sorgat it is 8 km, a 3–4 h climb; the climb to Bagatash Pass is extra. Altitude ~2000 m.
when: Season — late May / from 25 May to October; optimal mid-June to mid-August, especially July; in August there are night frosts. In winter — only snowmobile tours.
hours: A natural site; tours depart from Elekmonar at 07:00 (a group on a GAZ-66) or 08:00 (jeep tour), returning in the evening (Karakol-Tur, 2026).
daytime: Midday — the sun is above the cirques and the lakes glow (editorial); for stars — an overnight stay at the tourist base.
how: Gorno-Altaysk — Elekmonar via the Chuysky and Chemal trakts (~99 km, by bus ~2 h, the buses to Chemal pass through Elekmonar). From Elekmonar — only all-terrain trucks (GAZ-66, ZIL-130, UAZ) for about 30–33 km along the bed and valley of the Elekmonar (20+ fords) to the Sorgat tract (~3 h), then 8–12 km uphill: on foot (3–4 h), on horseback or by GAZ-66 (1.5–3 h). In your own regular car — not possible. Approaches from the Beshpeltir/Kuyum side are not described in the sources found.
needcar: Yes — an organized all-terrain truck (GAZ-66/UAZ) from Elekmonar or Chemal; or on foot/horseback over several days.
self: On foot — yes (for experienced hikers, over several days, with fords across the Elekmonar). By car — only in your own serious 4×4; most people go with local all-terrain trucks.
roadtype: Paved to Elekmonar; Elekmonar — Sorgat is heavy off-road along the riverbed, 20+ fords, bridges get washed away; higher up — a rocky track/trail.
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Elekmonar ~2 h; Elekmonar — lakes 3–4 h by all-terrain truck each way; the whole tour 12–14 h.
stay: The only tourist base is at the 5th lake (cedar cabins, a canteen, no mains power): a 2-day/1-night tour is 14,000 ₽ (Karakol-Tur, 2026); per tonkosti — 4,000–8,000 ₽/night, banya 1,500 ₽/h, a tent pitch 500 ₽, firewood 500 ₽ (year not stated). Bases in Elekmonar and Chemal.
net: not found (according to reviews there is no signal; check)
entry: No separate ticket found. The lakes are a regional natural monument; from 01.07.2026 the fee for visiting regional protected areas of the Altai Republic is 300 ₽ (residents of the Altai Republic keep the previous rate), but whether the Karakol Lakes are on the paid list was not found.
transfer: 4,000–6,000 ₽ per person (all-terrain truck/jeep from Elekmonar, 2026); 7,000 ₽ from Gorno-Altaysk (Sputnik8).
bring: A warm jacket/down jacket, a hat, a rain jacket (hail, downpours), trekking shoes, dry rations and water (food at the base is expensive; lunch ~1,000 ₽), tick repellent, motion-sickness pills, a headlamp if staying overnight.
warn: Fords across the Elekmonar — after rain and during floods the road may be impassable; the “shishiga” shakes you a lot. Altitude ~2000 m: down to 0 °C at night, snow on the upper lakes in July, hail. Ticks (in 2026, 22 cases of encephalitis in the Altai Republic). Children — from 5 years old (tour operators).
food: Lunch at the tourist base at the 5th lake — porridges, soups, dishes cooked in cauldrons over a fire (~1,000 ₽ per Karakol-Tur); in Chemal and Elekmonar — cafes with Altai cuisine (names not specified).
reviews: Sputnik8 (excursion from Gorno-Altaysk): 4.6/5, 11 reviews. Pluses — beauty, “like another world”, the starry sky. Minuses — a very hard road (4 h each way), cold, expensive food. 2GIS/Yandex ratings were not found.

p.sum: You go to Elekmonar (2 h from Gorno-Altaysk), and from there at 7 am a GAZ-66 or UAZ all-terrain truck takes ~3–4 h along the riverbed to the lakes; on site 3–4 hours to walk the chain of lakes and to Bagatash Pass, and back in the evening. Better — with an overnight stay at the tourist base at the 5th lake.
